blocks.title: Welcome.
blocks.sub: This website was made with Sitewright.

blocks.html:
Sitewright is a free simple webpage creator that generates webpages that host on GitHub. Inspiration is from Google Sites, an easy to use website creator that hosts pages on google drive. 

Sitewright works in a similar way to Google Sites, webpage creation is simple, no coding is required and a website can be created in minutes. All your site files are stored in your own GitHub repository. All you needs is a free GitHub account and do a little admin before a site can be created. SOUNDS LIKE HARD WORK!!!... Not at all, take a look at the instructions page for a step by step walk through.

Why did I make something that does essentially the same thing as Google Sites? Well it is a good question! I suppose Google Sites pages are locked to google drive, it's difficult to view the HTML files and make them usable in other places. Sitewright makes simple HTML websites where all the files are saved in GitHub. The HTML files can be saved, edited, shared and moved around freely. When or if you feel the need, editing HTML can be done directly through GitHub. 

Sitewright builds a professional looking, simple website that is fully functional and could be extended directly through the GitHub repository or other more advanced editors.

The other pages on the site will show examples of what Sitewright can do. Take a look, get inspired and make your own site. 
What your website be about and what will be on your home page?

1. Create the repo first On github.com, click New repository, name it (for example my-site), and tick Add a README so the repo has a main branch. Fine-grained tokens can only be limited to repos that already exist.

  2. Open token settings Click your profile photo, then Settings. At the bottom of the left sidebar choose Developer settings, then Personal access tokens, then Fine-grained tokens.

  3. Generate new token Click Generate new token. Give it a name like Sitewright, and set an expiry (30 to 90 days is a sensible choice).

  4. Limit it to your site repo Under Repository access, choose Only select repositories and pick the repo from step 1. This keeps the token from touching anything else on your account.

  5. Set the permissions Under Permissions, open Repository permissions and set Contents to Read and write, and Pages to Read and write. Metadata (read) is added automatically. You don't need Administration unless you want the tool to create repos.

  6. Generate and copy it Click Generate token, then copy the token that starts with github_pat_. GitHub only shows it once. Paste it into Sitewright's GitHub settings along with yourname/my-site.

Great, click the image button in the editor panel and choose an image file from your folders.
